obligations.description: Fixed STRLEN=0, PS2DIV=100, ROM_DIRECT_UPLOAD=0. SS high resets the SPI bit/10-bit byte counters, MISO is Z, and the response is preloaded with A4; falling edges shift out bits MSB first, rising edges sample MOSI, and the 8th bit forms a byte. The SPI byte count saturates at 1023, and conf_addr is this count. The byte-completion toggle passes through two-stage synchronization in sys/sd and is processed when the two synchronization bits differ; the local byte counters in the two domains each saturate at 255 and clear to 0 after the end of SS is synchronized. Hold the input between bits, and allow completed bytes to span enough sys/sd edges to avoid losing toggle events; under this contract the SPI half-period is at least 50ns, the sys period is 10ns, the sd period is 14ns, and SS is high for at least 400ns. There is no global reset port.

obligations.description: At each byte end for command 14, conf_chr is sampled as the next response; STRLEN=0 uses the external RAM input. Responses after command 16 are, in order, {6,sd_conf,sd_sdhc,sd_wr[drive],sd_rd[drive]}, the 8-bit value of drive, the four LBA bytes from highest to lowest, then 0. drive=sd_rd[1]|sd_wr[1]; LBA/drive are latched at the end of the command byte, and subsequent changes do not affect this transaction's snapshot. The next response for command 18 is sd_din at that time. Subsequent responses for undefined commands are 0.

obligations.description: Each payload of command 01 overwrites the control word: bits 1:0 are buttons, 3:2 are switches, 4 is scandoubler disable, 5 is ypbpr, and 6 is no_csync; bit 7 is ignored. 60–64 respectively update five 32-bit joysticks; the first four payloads write bits 7:0/15:8/23:16/31:24 in order, and other payloads are ignored; partial transactions modify only the bytes sent, uninitialized portions are X, and initialized portions not written retain their values.

obligations.description: Each payload of 15 overwrites the entire 32-bit status with an 8-bit value zero-extended; the first four payloads of 1E update the 32-bit status byte by byte in little-endian order, and the rest are ignored. Each payload of 21 writes the low 7 bits of core_mod. The first eight payloads of 22 update the 64-bit rtc byte by byte in little-endian order, with no BCD or date validation; extras are ignored. There are no relevant power-up initial values; portions retain their values after writes. A rise of status[0] flushes both serial read and write pointers simultaneously, and holding it at 1 inhibits serial writes.

obligations.description: Each payload of 05 enters keyboard processing; at the start of the first payload, pressed defaults to 1 and extended defaults to 0. E0 sets extended, and F0 clears pressed; an ordinary code emits key_code, with key_extended=previous extended AND not the first payload, and key_pressed=previous pressed OR the first payload. A prefix itself does not emit key_strobe; an ordinary code emits a one-cycle pulse on the processing sys edge, cleared on the next sys edge. The first ordinary code of a new transaction is always a non-extended make and does not inherit an old prefix.

Fewer than four bytes do not publish, and extra bytes do not publish again.

obligations.description: The 17/18 commands assert sd_ack when received in the sd domain; 19 asserts sd_ack_conf. Each payload of 17/19 produces a one-cycle sd_dout_strobe and outputs that byte; the next sd edge clears strobe and increments the 9-bit address by 1, with the address saturating at 511 rather than wrapping around. After the end of SS is synchronized, ack and both strobes are cleared and the address is cleared to 0; sd_dout retains its last value.

obligations.description: The 18 command and subsequent payloads request the next sd_din: command processing first strobes and increments address 0 by 1, and thereafter strobes again and increments by 1 only when address!=511. The MISO response samples sd_din at the SPI byte end, independently of the sd-domain strobe. A rising edge of sd_wr[0] triggers address 0 and din_strobe in the sd domain; a rise of sd_wr[1] alone does not trigger this prefetch. The end of SS takes priority in clearing the address and strobe.

obligations.description: Each payload of 1C selects img_mounted[0/1] according to its least significant bit and sets it to 1; it clears by default on the next sd edge, and the two bits can pulse individually on consecutive events. The first four payloads of 1D write the 32-bit img_size in little-endian order; partial transactions preserve other bytes, and additional bytes are ignored. Mounting does not automatically clear size.

obligations.description: A rise of serial_strobe writes serial_data into a 64-entry ring, with the write pointer modulo 64 and no full detection; equal read and write pointers indicate empty, so writing a full 64 entries appears empty. A rise of status[0] clears both pointers. 1B responses alternate according to byte-count parity: the first response after the command is the current read byte, followed by {1000000,available}, continuing to alternate data/flags; the read pointer advances only on the SPI falling edge at the end of a nonzero even-numbered byte and only if data is available. The data storage itself is not guaranteed to be 0 when empty.

obligations.description: The fixed RTL has no reset or initial values for the PS2 divider count, clock, transmit state, or FIFO pointers; these states remain unknown at native four-state startup, and valid serial frames cannot be promised on the four PS2 outputs. Do not force internal clocks or add reset to them. The keyboard/mouse structured event ports remain testable under the command contracts above; unknown PS2 states cannot be generalized to mean that other outputs need not be checked.

dv-033-obligation-1.description: Start with SS high for 400ns; in each transaction transmit the command MSB first and 0/1/4/255/256/1023/1030 payloads using a 50ns half-period, interrupting with SS and then restarting.

dv-033-obligation-2.description: Vary conf_chr and the sd drive0/1 read/write combinations, change LBA/drive after command 16 to verify the snapshot, go beyond the end of the response, and send unknown commands.

dv-033-obligation-3.description: Send 1, 2, 4, and 6 bytes to each of the five joystick groups, alternating all-0/all-1 and seed-mixed bytes; cover all 7 bits of the buttons and overwriting with multiple payloads.

dv-033-obligation-4.description: Send index0–15 individually, with separate X/Y updates and truncated transactions, and append extra payloads.

dv-033-obligation-5.description: First establish known values byte by byte, then mix 15/1E partial overwrites, core bit7, RTC non-BCD data, and overlength payloads; set status0 to 1 and then clear it to 0.

dv-033-obligation-6.description: Ordinary initial codes, E0/F0 combinations, repeated prefixes, multiple ordinary codes in the same frame, an ordinary code starting a new frame after E0 in the preceding frame, and truncated prefixes.

dv-033-obligation-7.description: All flags sign combinations for 70/71, X/Y boundaries, ignoring the upper 4 bits of Z, and 3/4/5-byte lengths.

dv-033-obligation-8.description: Send 0, 1, multiple bytes, and more than 512 bytes for each of 17/19, and observe synchronized clearing on SS deassertion; alternate commands and interrupt transactions.

dv-033-obligation-9.description: Upload more than 512 bytes, vary sd_din with input history, and change the two sd_wr bits separately; combine these with SS termination and byte processing on the same edge.

dv-033-obligation-10.description: Two drives, irrelevant upper payload bits, partial size, four-byte boundaries and extra bytes, and alternating size writes before and after mounting.

dv-033-obligation-11.description: After reset by status, write 0/1/63/64/65 bytes, alternate flag/data reads, read beyond empty, write during reads, and flush again with status.

dv-033-obligation-12.description: Use native power-up without force, run the sys clock and send keyboard/mouse data, while also checking structured events.

policy: Fixed obligations for this problem × five dimensions, with claims deduplicated by semantics and local impacts; scoring is not based on test names/counts.
strategy_policy: Assess the five dimensions per obligation over legal input histories and genuine observation windows. An expected value describes the full-domain oracle and does not broaden the actual stimulus; narrow stimuli only lose credit for missing dimensions. Incorrect sampling does not automatically mean that actual copies expected. No specific values are promised for uninitialized portions, and this cannot be generalized to defined outputs. Other equivalent executable strategies are allowed; there are no fixed ordering or sample-count requirements.
